forward_vs_spot.interpretation: The forward curve prices roughly 1.4-1.5% of annualised dollar depreciation at every tenor, which is simply the 137.5bp policy differential expressed as points - a long-dollar spot position pays that hurdle continuously whether or not it is right. Our edge decays sharply with horizon, from 140 pips at one month to 51 at three and 24 at six, and that decay profile IS the horizon split expressed in pips: we think the market underprices the September hike and we do not think it materially misprices anything beyond December. The practical consequence is that the trade should be sized and structured for one month, not six, and that at three and six months the residual edge of 51 and 24 pips is smaller than the bid-offer plus carry cost of maintaining the position - which is another way of saying the strategic stance is genuinely Neutral rather than quietly bullish.

key_catalysts.event: Bank of Canada rate decision, RBNZ Monetary Policy Statement, and Federal Reserve Beige Book
key_catalysts.rationale: Three events on one day, all of which widen or confirm the dollar's differential. The Bank of Canada is expected to hold at 2.25%, leaving a 137.5bp dollar premium intact, and the RBNZ is expected to hold at 2.50%. The Beige Book is the first anecdotal read on whether the July payroll contraction is showing up in regional business conditions, which is the labour-market question the September decision turns on.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Fully for the two rate holds; not priced for the Beige Book's labour commentary, which has no consensus attached
key_catalysts.bilateral_relevance: USD/CAD and NZD/USD directly; the Beige Book affects the whole dollar complex

key_catalysts.event: US trade balance, ISM Services PMI, and Fed Governor Waller speech
key_catalysts.rationale: The trade balance is forecast at -$86.4bn after -$73.3bn, and the advance goods figure already missed by $18bn at -$118.8bn, so a second large miss would be the first tactically relevant external datapoint of the cycle. ISM Services is forecast at 54.1 with the prices sub-index at 70.3 and the employment sub-index at 47.4 - inflationary and contractionary simultaneously, which is the dossier's central tension in one release.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Partially - the ISM headline has a consensus but the employment and prices sub-indices do not, and those carry the signal
key_catalysts.bilateral_relevance: EUR/USD and the broad dollar; the trade figure matters for the strategic external-balance view

key_catalysts.event: August US non-farm payrolls, unemployment rate and average hourly earnings
key_catalysts.rationale: The single largest data risk before the FOMC. Consensus is +58,000 headline and +50,000 private after July's -23,000, with unemployment at 4.1% and average hourly earnings at +0.3% on the month against a year-on-year rate of 3.2%, a five-year low. A second consecutive contraction would make a 16 September hike very difficult to defend and would strand a net long position of 18,682 contracts.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Partially - the headline has a firm +58,000 consensus, but the market has not priced the conditional path from a negative print to a Fed hold twelve days later
key_catalysts.bilateral_relevance: EUR/USD and USD/JPY carry the largest reaction; GBP/USD is most sensitive because the differential sign changes

key_catalysts.rationale: Brent has fallen from a $105.32 July peak through $100.31 to $88.24 and was rebounding on 1 September on Middle East risk. For a net energy exporter the direct dollar effect of higher oil is mildly positive through terms of trade, but the larger effect runs through inflation, where higher energy prices reinforce the hawkish case ten days before the FOMC.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Not priced - no consensus is published for OPEC outcomes and the volatility term structure carries no premium around the date
key_catalysts.bilateral_relevance: USD/CAD and USD/NOK most directly; second-order for EUR/USD via the inflation channel

key_catalysts.event: ECB Governing Council decision with staff projections; US PPI
key_catalysts.rationale: The ECB is expected to hold at 2.25% with a full projection round attached. Euro-area headline inflation at 3.3% on the August flash with core at 2.5% gives the Governing Council no reason to tighten, so the 137.5bp differential is confirmed rather than challenged - and confirmation from the other side of a 57.6% DXY weight matters more than most US data.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Fully for the hold; the projections are not priced and are the part that could move the differential
key_catalysts.bilateral_relevance: EUR/USD directly, and through it the DXY

key_catalysts.event: US August CPI; University of Michigan preliminary; monthly federal budget balance
key_catalysts.rationale: The last inflation print before the FOMC, against a July base of 3.4% headline and 2.5% core. The unusual configuration is that core CPI at 2.5% sits 80bp BELOW core PCE at 3.3%, so a soft core CPI print would be less dovish than it appears - the Fed targets PCE, and Warsh's 28 August speech quoted headline PCE at 3.7% and 4.1% on six months. The budget balance follows a prior print of -$432bn.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Partially - the CPI has no published consensus in the cached calendar, and the market has not internalised that the core CPI to core PCE wedge is inverted
key_catalysts.bilateral_relevance: EUR/USD and USD/JPY; the budget figure matters for the strategic fiscal view

key_catalysts.event: FOMC decision, Summary of Economic Projections and press conference; Treasury TIC data
key_catalysts.rationale: The dominant event in the dossier. Fed funds futures price roughly 57-66% odds of a 25bp hike to 3.75-4.00% while the June dot plot's 2026 median of 3.8% implies it outright and prediction markets carry it at roughly 48-55%. The dot plot released alongside also resets the strategic path, since the 2027 median of 3.6% currently makes the move terminal. TIC data lands the same day after a prior net long-term inflow of $172.7bn.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Partially - 57-66% of the hike is in futures, leaving 34-43% unpriced, and the volatility term structure is in contango rather than backwardation, so the event itself carries almost no premium
key_catalysts.bilateral_relevance: Every dollar pair; GBP/USD sees a differential sign change and USD/JPY has the largest carry sensitivity

key_catalysts.rationale: The Bank is expected to hold at 3.75% the day after the FOMC. If the Fed hikes, the dollar-sterling policy differential flips from -12.5bp to +12.5bp, making the dollar the higher-yielding leg against sterling for the first time this cycle. That is the cleanest sign change available in the G10 and it lands within 24 hours of the Fed.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Fully for the BoE hold; the differential sign change is conditional on the Fed and is not separately priced
key_catalysts.bilateral_relevance: GBP/USD, and EUR/GBP as the cross-market expression

key_catalysts.event: Bank of Japan Monetary Policy Meeting
key_catalysts.rationale: The BoJ is expected to hold at 1.00%, leaving a 262.5bp policy differential, two days after the Fed. USD/JPY at 159.746 sits at the 77th percentile of its 52-week range and is the most carry-sensitive pair in the set, so a BoJ hold immediately after a Fed hike widens the differential at the exact moment the pair is most extended.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Fully for the hold; the risk is a hawkish surprise, since the cached Japanese 10-year of 2.67% is a stale June vintage that understates the live level
key_catalysts.bilateral_relevance: USD/JPY overwhelmingly; second-order for the DXY at a 13.6% weight

key_catalysts.event: Swiss National Bank quarterly assessment, Norges Bank Monetary Policy Report and Riksbank Monetary Policy Report - all on the same day
key_catalysts.rationale: Three European central banks report simultaneously. The SNB is anchored at zero, leaving the dollar's largest carry advantage at 362.5bp untouched; Norges Bank at 4.25% faces a Brent price $12 lower on the month; the Riksbank sits at a 1.75% trough with inflation near zero. None is expected to move, so the day confirms rather than changes the differential map.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Fully - all three are expected to hold and none carries meaningful option premium
key_catalysts.bilateral_relevance: USD/CHF, USD/NOK and USD/SEK; immaterial for the DXY beyond the 3.6% Swiss and 4.2% Swedish weights

key_catalysts.event: Reserve Bank of Australia Monetary Policy Board decision
key_catalysts.rationale: The RBA is expected to hold at 4.35%, the highest policy rate in the set and 72.5bp above the dollar. Australian CPI at 3.96% on the cached OECD measure keeps the Board from cutting, so the dollar's worst carry position is confirmed rather than relieved, and AUD/USD is already at the 87th percentile of its 52-week range.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Fully for the hold; what is not priced is how long the RBA can sustain a rate above the Fed's if the Fed hikes
key_catalysts.bilateral_relevance: AUD/USD, which is the pair where a long-dollar view is paid to be wrong

key_catalysts.event: September quarter-end US dollar funding date
key_catalysts.rationale: The first quarter-end since reserve balances resumed falling, at $2,916bn and heading toward the roughly $3 trillion minimum comfortable level, with the overnight reverse repo facility drained to $702 million. Quarter-end balance-sheet management routinely tightens repo, and there is no buffer left to absorb it. The December 2025 precedent saw standing repo usage reach a record $74.6 billion on 31 December 2025.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Not priced at all - the cross-currency basis at -0.81bp shows nobody is hedging a funding event, and no volatility premium exists around the date
key_catalysts.bilateral_relevance: All dollar pairs simultaneously; funding stress is the one channel that moves the whole complex together

key_catalysts.event: FOMC decision without a Summary of Economic Projections
key_catalysts.rationale: The first meeting after September with no dot plot attached, which makes it the moment the market must judge on the Committee's silence whether the September move was terminal. This is our identified inflection point between the tactical and strategic horizons.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Not priced - it is beyond the tactical window and the six-month volatility term structure at 5.834% carries no event premium
key_catalysts.bilateral_relevance: EUR/USD principally; the whole complex if the statement language shifts

key_catalysts.rationale: The dominant scheduled event of the strategic window and genuinely two-sided. A result that constrains fiscal expansion is dollar-positive through the deficit channel and negative through growth; a result that enables it is the reverse. The second-order question of how the outcome changes political pressure on a Federal Reserve that has just hiked over presidential objection is unknowable in advance.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Not priced. No volatility premium exists at any tenor covering the date, which for an event of this size is itself notable
key_catalysts.bilateral_relevance: The broad dollar rather than any single pair; the fiscal channel is expressed in the long end and in USD/JPY

key_catalysts.event: FOMC decision with Summary of Economic Projections
key_catalysts.rationale: The final Fed event of the strategic window and the release at which the 2027 median dot - currently 3.6%, implying a cut back from a September hike - is either confirmed or removed. Confirmation validates the strategic Neutral; removal would convert the September move from terminal into a cycle and would be the trigger to upgrade the strategic stance.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Not priced - the December meeting sits beyond any tenor carrying an event premium in the current contango term structure
key_catalysts.bilateral_relevance: EUR/USD and USD/JPY; the dot plot is the specific release that determines the strategic path

key_catalysts.rationale: The direct analogue of the December 2025 episode, when SOFR-to-IORB spreads reached their widest since 2020 and standing repo usage spiked to a record $74.6 billion on 31 December 2025, before collapsing to zero in early January. Every precondition is in place and several are worse, though the rebranded standing repo operations with no aggregate limit should cap the tail at pressure rather than crisis.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Not priced - a cross-currency basis of -0.81bp says the market carries no year-end funding hedge whatsoever
key_catalysts.bilateral_relevance: All dollar pairs; the effect is broad rather than bilateral, and it is the principal strategic dollar positive

key_catalysts.event: IMF COFER release for 2026-Q2 reserve currency composition
key_catalysts.rationale: The quarterly measure of whether the dollar's reserve share resumes eroding. It printed 57.13% in 2026-Q1, UP from a 56.42% fourth quarter that was the first sub-57% reading since 1995, so the most recent observation cuts against the de-dollarisation thesis. The critical detail to read is the decomposition: a recent quarter saw 92% of the decline attributable to valuation effects rather than active selling, and a print in which active selling dominates would be a materially different signal.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Not priced. COFER is a lagged quarterly statistic that no forecast we could source treats as a dollar driver
key_catalysts.bilateral_relevance: The broad trade-weighted dollar rather than G10 bilaterals; consistent with the broad index falling 1.69% against the G10 basket's 0.37%

invalidators.condition: The FOMC holds the target range at 3.50-3.75% on 16 September 2026 rather than hiking
invalidators.mechanism: A hold strands a net long of 18,682 contracts in a market that repriced from 35.4% to 60.4% hike odds in four sessions, and it simultaneously destroys the guidance premium built on a June dot plot median of 3.8%. The tactical thesis is 78% dependent on Factors 1 and 2, both of which resolve on this date.
invalidators.monitor_indicator: FOMC statement and implementation note; fed funds futures-implied probability in the preceding fortnight
invalidators.monitor_frequency: Daily until 16 September, then at the 2pm ET release
invalidators.quantitative_threshold: Target range unchanged at 3.50-3.75%, or futures-implied hike probability falling below 40% before the meeting

invalidators.condition: August non-farm payrolls on 4 September print negative for a second consecutive month
invalidators.mechanism: Two consecutive contractions would make a hike twelve days later analytically indefensible and would convert the labour-market weakness in Factor 2 from a caveat into the dominant read. The Committee cannot tighten into a visibly contracting labour market without inviting exactly the policy-mistake pricing that the strategic downside case describes.
invalidators.monitor_indicator: BLS Employment Situation report, headline non-farm payrolls
invalidators.quantitative_threshold: Headline payrolls below zero, against a +58,000 consensus

invalidators.condition: The three-month EUR/USD cross-currency basis moves beyond minus 30 basis points
invalidators.mechanism: This invalidates the CHARACTER of the thesis rather than its direction. A genuine dollar funding premium would move the currency from the right-hand exceptionalism side of the smile to the left-hand stress side, at which point the dollar strengthens for reasons that have nothing to do with the rate differential and the tactical rates-based framework stops being the right lens.
invalidators.quantitative_threshold: Below -30bp for three consecutive sessions, against -0.81bp on 2026-08-28

invalidators.condition: Core PCE falls below 3.0% year on year in the September or October release
invalidators.mechanism: Core PCE at 3.3% for three consecutive months is the stickiest of the inflation series and the analytical justification for tightening into a weakening labour market; note that Warsh's own speech cited headline PCE at 3.7% and 4.1% on six months rather than the core measure. A move below 3.0% would let the Committee declare the tariff impulse transitory and remove the reaction-function basis for further tightening, collapsing Factors 1, 2 and 6 together.
invalidators.monitor_indicator: BEA Personal Income and Outlays, core PCE price index year on year
invalidators.monitor_frequency: Monthly, roughly four weeks after the reference month
invalidators.quantitative_threshold: Core PCE below 3.0% year on year, against 3.3% in July 2026

invalidators.condition: EUR/USD closes above 1.16339, the 200-day moving average, on a weekly basis
invalidators.mechanism: The moving-average configuration is stacked dollar-bullish but tangled, with the 50-day, 100-day and 200-day within 1.24% of each other and spot sitting between the 100-day and the 200-day. A weekly close above the 200-day resolves the tangle against the dollar and converts systematic trend-following capital from neutral into a seller, adding a flow amplifier to whatever fundamental move caused it.
invalidators.monitor_indicator: EUR/USD weekly close versus the 200-day simple moving average

invalidators.condition: A US long-end Treasury auction fails or tails severely, with the 30-year clearing above 5.50%
invalidators.mechanism: This is the specific event that converts the fiscal position from a term-premium story into a currency story. Auction reception is already deteriorating - the 20-year stopped at 5.204% against 5.163% and the 30-year TIPS at 2.973% against 2.473%, a 50bp jump - and a clear failure would signal that foreign official demand is withdrawing at the same time as the reserve share resumes falling, which is the twin-deficit configuration in which fiscal gravity actually applies.
invalidators.monitor_indicator: Treasury auction results: stop-out yield, bid-to-cover, and indirect bidder share
invalidators.monitor_frequency: Per auction, per the Treasury quarterly refunding schedule

invalidators.condition: The 16 September dot plot lifts the 2027 median above 3.6%, removing the implied cut
invalidators.mechanism: This invalidates the STRATEGIC Neutral rather than the tactical Bullish. The entire horizon split rests on the Committee's own June projections making the September hike terminal - a 2026 median of 3.8% followed by 3.6% in 2027. Removing that cut converts a terminal hike into a cycle and would justify carrying the tactical position into the strategic window rather than treating it as having an expiry.
invalidators.monitor_indicator: FOMC Summary of Economic Projections, median federal funds rate for 2027
invalidators.monitor_frequency: Quarterly, at the March, June, September and December meetings
invalidators.quantitative_threshold: 2027 median above 3.6%, against 3.6% in the June 2026 SEP

invalidators.condition: The tariff structure is unwound with refunds following the lapse of Section 122 authority

Unwinding it deflates the goods component mechanically, removes the case for further hikes, and creates a contingent fiscal refund liability of uncertain size at the same time.

factors_changed.reason: Core PCE has now held at 3.3% for three consecutive months and headline PCE beat forecast at 3.7%, while Q2 core PCE deflators came in above consensus at 3.6% annualised. The tactical read moves from Neutral to Bullish because the Fed has explicitly tied its reaction function to this measure. Strategically the stance improves from Bearish to Neutral because the growth side firmed - composite PMI 56.0 and GDPNow 4.6% - even as the labour side deteriorated.

The VIX collapsed from 20.66 to 14.43 and high-yield spreads tightened 27bp to 260bp. Mechanically that is dollar-negative under the inverted sign convention, but it is offset by live US exceptionalism, so the tactical stance moves from Bearish to Neutral rather than deeper into negative territory.

A clean reversal in both directions. Tactically the stance improves because speculative length has been cut for four consecutive weeks from a three-and-a-half-year high, and all of that reduction predated Jackson Hole. Strategically it worsens because the reserve share touched a three-decade low of 56.42% in 2025-Q4 before rebounding to 57.13%, and the starting position is a multi-year high, so the medium-term distribution of change is one-way.

The largest stance change in the dossier and the one that drives the strategic downgrade. Brent has fallen from a $105.32 July peak to $88.24, removing the energy-export support that justified the prior Bullish reading, the goods trade balance deteriorated $18bn in a single month to -$118.8bn, and the primary income balance flipped from surplus to deficit.

Stance unchanged on both horizons; tactical confidence rises five points because the 16 September FOMC now carries a live 57-66% hike probability with a dot plot attached, which is a far more tractable event than the diffuse geopolitical risk that dominated the prior report.

Stance unchanged and strategic confidence essentially unchanged, but tactical confidence falls ten points because the transmission has visibly inverted: on 1 September a global bond rout lifted yields and the dollar together, so a deteriorating fiscal position is currently expressed as dollar-supportive rather than dollar-destructive.

The tactical stance reverses from Bearish to Bullish because EUR/USD is now sitting precisely on the 1.15904 upper bound of a five-touch demand zone with the moving averages stacked dollar-bullish, and because the volatility term structure is in contango fifteen days before a binary FOMC - a structural and expression advantage that did not exist a month ago.

The horizons swap. Tactically the stance falls to Neutral because a cross-currency basis of -0.81bp confirms there is no funding premium at all today. Strategically it rises to Bullish because reserve balances have resumed falling to $2,916bn with the reverse repo facility drained to $702 million, reproducing the preconditions of the December 2025 squeeze inside the six-month window.

signposts_triggered.outcome: Triggered decisively. Market-implied September hike odds moved from 35.4% on 27 August to roughly 57.5% on 28 August and 60.4% by 31 August following Chair Warsh's Jackson Hole keynote.
signposts_triggered.implication: The single largest change since the prior report. The dollar's driver has shifted from a passive rate-level advantage to an active tightening expectation, which is why the tactical net score more than doubled from +0.1477 to +0.3440.

signposts_triggered.implication: The energy-led global inflation shock that framed the August dossier has substantially unwound. That removes the terms-of-trade support behind the prior Bullish external-balance stance and is the proximate reason Factor 5 was downgraded to strategically Bearish.

conviction_change.explanation: Tactical conviction rises from 2 to 3 and the tactical net score more than doubles from +0.1477 to +0.3440, taking the dollar from fifth of eleven to first of eleven. The entire increase is attributable to the Federal Reserve becoming the only G10 central bank expected to tighten, confirmed by a 9-3 July vote with three hawkish dissents and by Warsh's 28 August keynote. Strategic conviction is unchanged at 2 but the net stance changes from Bullish to Neutral and the score falls from +0.2079 to +0.1032, dropping the dollar from fourth to fourth on rank but from a directional view to a balanced one - because External Balance swung from Bullish to Bearish at a 0.16 weight as the energy shock unwound and the primary income balance turned negative.

seasonality.pattern: Two documented and currently relevant patterns. First, US dollar year-end funding pressure: bank balance-sheet management around the turn of the year systematically tightens repo markets, and the December 2025 episode saw SOFR-to-IORB spreads reach their widest since 2020 and standing repo usage print $25.95 billion on 29 December and spike to a record $74.6 billion on 31 December before collapsing to zero in early January. Second, Japanese fiscal half-year-end repatriation flows at the end of September, which are a documented seasonal support for the yen and therefore a headwind for USD/JPY.
seasonality.relevance_window: The September Japanese half-year-end falls squarely inside the tactical window and coincides with the 18 September Bank of Japan meeting. The year-end funding turn falls in the last month of the strategic window and is treated as a dated catalyst in its own right.
seasonality.historical_magnitude: The December 2025 funding episode is the only precedent quantified in this dossier: a record $74.6 billion of standing repo usage on 31 December 2025 and the widest SOFR-IORB spreads since 2020, resolving within roughly four weeks. No reliable magnitude estimate for the Japanese repatriation effect was sourced this run, and it is therefore noted as a directional pattern only rather than being assigned a size.
seasonality.current_alignment: The two patterns point in opposite directions and both are aligned with their historical seasonal sign. The September Japanese flow works against the tactical long-dollar view specifically in USD/JPY, which is already at the 77th percentile of its 52-week range on a stale yield spread - a reason to prefer USD/CAD or USD/CHF as the tactical expression. The year-end funding pattern works for the strategic Bullish reading of Factor 10 and is the principal reason that factor carries a positive strategic contribution.

assumptions: The market-implied probability of a 25bp hike on 16 September is quoted as a RANGE of roughly 57-66% rather than a point estimate. CME FedWatch has no citable URL, and the sources disagree materially: 60.4% on 31 August in one report, 'nearly 56%' in another on 28 August, and 66% in a third on 31 August, while prediction markets carry it at roughly 48-55%. That venue divergence is reported as a finding rather than averaged away.

All peer sovereign 10-year yields in this dossier are cached MONTHLY observations dated 2026-06-01 and are known from this cycle's cross-checks to understate live levels materially - peers measured 35-47bp too low against 2 September vendor quotes elsewhere in the cycle, and Japan's live 10-year was 3.017% against a cached 2.67%. Every long-end spread is therefore computed with BOTH legs at the same June vintage so the comparison is internally consistent, and is explicitly labelled as a vintage comparison rather than a live spread. Only the US DGS series is current and reliable.

The PPP deviation table is NOT sourced from OECD or World Bank purchasing power parity data, for which no free source was obtainable this run. It is constructed as a proxy from BIS real effective exchange rate relatives for June 2026 - the ratio of the dollar's REER of 107.84 to each peer's REER, minus one - and the implied fair values are the current spot rate adjusted by that deviation. This is a real-exchange-rate relative, not a PPP estimate, and it should not be read as one.

The BIS REER historical percentile of 78 and the one-year implied volatility percentile of 22 are internal estimates rather than published statistics. The REER percentile is estimated against the post-2015 range; the implied volatility percentile is inferred from the absolute level of EUR/USD three-month at-the-money implied volatility at 5.679% relative to the post-2022 range. Neither should be quoted as a source figure.

All CFTC positioning data is web-sourced because the pipeline's cached Commitments of Traders file contains no Dollar Index contract. The DXY contract is reported as non-commercial versus commercial rather than with the leveraged-fund and asset-manager split available for the major bilateral contracts, so the same non-commercial net figure of 18,682 appears in both schema fields - that is a reporting limitation, not two independent observations. The positioning percentile of 80 is an internal estimate anchored on the reported 'three-and-a-half-year high' description of the 22,499-contract peak.

Twenty-five delta risk reversals could not be obtained from any free source and are recorded as an explicit gap. UUP and UDN exchange-traded fund flows are likewise unavailable. The options skew channel is therefore uninformed rather than neutral, and no skew-dependent conclusion is drawn anywhere in this dossier.

Implied volatility is taken from CME at-the-money quotes observed on 2026-08-26 at tenors of 43.6, 99.6 and 190.6 days, which are treated as the one-month, three-month and six-month points. Realised volatility is read directly from the pipeline's derived store rather than recomputed, and is annualised on 252 weekday observations. Carry-to-volatility ratios are stated as annualised carry in per cent divided by 60-day realised volatility in per cent, not against implied volatility.

No rating-agency page was directly fetchable this run because all three are JavaScript-rendered. The Moody's Aa1, S&P AA+ and Fitch AA+ ratings and their stable outlooks are taken from secondary reporting and are marked best available and flagged.

Bank forecast levels other than MUFG's are aggregator-reported rather than first-party. The Morgan Stanley figure near 94 is a MID-2026 trough, not a year-end target - that bank's year-end 2026 number is 99, essentially spot - and the Natixis figure of 98 is end-2026. Both are attributed to the aggregator that published them and should not be treated as verified bank house views. The MUFG note is dated 19 December 2025, is premised on Fed cuts that did not occur, and breaches this dossier's own 60-day strategic freshness window; it is retained only because it is the sole first-party bank source obtainable.

The Singapore row of the macro comparison table is entirely web-sourced and is carried from this cycle's shared research layer, because Singapore is not an OECD member and the pipeline vintage store holds no Singapore observation. Singapore has no policy rate by design; the three-month compounded SORA figure near 1.40% used in the carry table is a money-market proxy and not a policy differential.

The dollar basket performance figures of -0.37%, -0.12%, +0.46% and +1.95% are computed by applying published DXY constituent weights to the cached pair performance figures, not read from a DXY series. They are a replication of the index rather than the index itself, and the Federal Reserve broad index at -1.69% over one month is reported alongside them because the two measures diverge materially.

The Section 122 authority for the 10% global tariff ran 150 days from 2026-02-24 and expired on 2026-07-24; Section 301 duties of 10-12.5% on roughly 80 trading partners, arising from the USTR determination of 2 June 2026, took effect the same day, with Section 232 actions in parallel. The tariff rate quoted throughout is the Yale Budget Lab average STATUTORY rate of 11.0% as at 2026-08-24, not an effective collected rate: Penn Wharton's effective measure was 7.1% in June 2026 and the Tax Foundation's applied measure 11.7%. The choice of measure materially changes the number and is therefore stated rather than assumed.

Seven citations to CNBC (ids 14-17 and 20) returned HTTP 200 with a zero-length body from this run's environment, which is an Akamai bot block rather than a dead link. Every factual claim they support is independently corroborated by a primary source cited alongside them - the Federal Reserve statement and speech, BEA and BLS releases - and no claim in this dossier rests on a CNBC page alone.

The IMF COFER figure was corrected during adversarial verification. The dollar's share of allocated reserves ROSE to 57.13% in 2026-Q1 from 56.42% in 2025-Q4; the sub-57% print, the first since 1995, was the fourth quarter of 2025, not the first quarter of 2026. The de-dollarisation leg of the strategic case is correspondingly weaker than a single-quarter reading would suggest, and the confidence on Factors 4 and 5 was reduced to reflect it.

The tariff rate was corrected during adversarial verification from a stale pre-ruling figure near 17% to the Yale Budget Lab average statutory rate of 11.0% as at 2026-08-24, and the Section 301 duties that replaced Section 122 on 2026-07-24 are in force rather than pending. Confidence on Factors 2, 5 and 7 was reduced accordingly.

The Atlanta Fed GDPNow figure is a live nowcast with no dated permalink. It is quoted at 4.8% as updated on 2026-09-01, against 4.6% on 2026-08-26; readers checking the source later will see a different number by construction.

Where a claim could not be confirmed against a fetchable source it is marked best available and flagged in text: the SOFR level (NY Fed page is JavaScript-rendered), the three rating-agency outlooks (all JavaScript-rendered), and the aggregator-reported bank forecasts.
